regulator: Arizona Department of Health Services (licensing); Arizona Department of Revenue (tax data)

data_source.name: ADOR: Arizona Marijuana TPT and Excise Taxable Sales and Tax Collections, by Period Covered
data_source.notes: Arizona does not publish tracked retail sales; these are the Department of Revenue's estimated taxable sales by period covered, from transaction privilege tax returns (medical = business code 203, adult_use = code 420). ADOR labels the figures estimated. August 2025 shows a negative medical figure (an adjustment), so medical and total are null for that month. Totals are adult-use plus medical. Annual figures are sums of the monthly figures.

monthly.note: ADOR reports a negative medical figure for this period (an adjustment); medical and total left null

annual.basis: sum of ADOR monthly estimated taxable sales
adult_use = sum of ADOR monthly estimated taxable sales; medical not summed because one month carries a negative adjustment

tax_note: Adult-use marijuana pays a 16% state marijuana excise tax plus state and local transaction privilege (sales) tax; medical marijuana pays only the transaction privilege tax (Arizona Department of Revenue).
summary: Arizona's adult-use market launched in January 2021 at existing medical dispensaries and quickly overtook the medical program. Taxable adult-use sales were $82.1 million in August 2026, against $9.8 million of medical sales. Adult-use sales have held near $1.07 billion a year in 2024 and 2025, while medical sales have fallen by more than half since 2022 as patients switch to adult-use stores, which removes the main price advantage of a medical card. Arizona's store count is capped, which limits competition between dispensaries but also caps access in fast-growing suburbs.

faq.q: How much cannabis does Arizona sell a month?
faq.a: The Department of Revenue estimates $82.1 million in taxable adult-use sales and $9.8 million in medical sales for August 2026, about $91.8 million in all.

faq.q: Are Arizona's cannabis sales figures exact?
faq.a: No. ADOR labels them estimated taxable sales, derived from tax returns by the period they cover, and they can be revised when returns are amended.

faq.q: Why are Arizona medical marijuana sales falling?
faq.a: Medical sales fell from $250.8 million in 2024 to about $10 million to $12 million a month in 2026 as patients shift to adult-use stores.
